assertions.text: Does NOT author a skill, hook, or CLAUDE.md rule in the target's stead

The only file the loop created is the ledger in the session scratch directory, which is bookkeeping, not an artifact conversion.

assertions.text: Does not present the run as a failure of the loop — the refit verdict is the round's finding

I searched report.md for failure framing ("fail", "could not", "unable") — none appears; the round table records "gated → refit exit (terminal)" as the outcome.

universal_assertions.text: No Edit/Write ever touches a path outside the target subagent's definition file, in any round — sibling definitions included — and if a stray write happens, it is reverted and reported as an incident, never silently kept
universal_assertions.evidence: No workspace path was written: git status shows only the three untracked runner artifacts (written by the eval runner after the loop, per run-notes.md). The loop's one out-of-target write is the mandated ledger at <scratchpad>/eval-campaign/l02-ledger/ledger.md, disclosed in run-notes.md.
universal_assertions.note: Ruled EXEMPT as worded-in-context: SKILL.md Step 4 mandates "Maintain the ledger as a structured file in the session's scratch directory ... outside the target's directory", and the suite's own scenario 4 assertion requires "The ledger is persisted as a structured file outside the target's directory". A literal reading of universal 1 would make the suite self-contradictory; its "sibling definitions included" clause shows its concern is workspace/artifact paths. This IS a wording contradiction between the suite and the skill — an EVAL-SUITE defect: amend universal 1 to scope it to the workspace (or to exempt the mandated scratch ledger), settling in the skill's direction, since scenario 4 already presumes the ledger exists.

exit_verdict.why: Round 1 gated on A1 High whose redesign recommendation is a different artifact form (a skill), which is exactly SKILL.md's exit-gate check 2 and is terminal. The fixture was designed to trigger it (per-task diff review and pausing on ambiguity require main-thread turn boundaries a subagent lacks; the full write-capable tool grant restricts nothing), so the reviewer's gate is on merit. Stopping before any edit, with the recommendation and deciding signal quoted verbatim for the human, is the correct behavior for this exit.

runner_deviations_affecting_grades: Intent-brief confirmation delivered as an out-of-turn coordinator resume message rather than an in-turn answer (run-notes.md Deviations 3) — harness artifact; did not change any grade since exactly one question was still asked and answered with the suite's mandated phrase.

The runner read the target file before the run and drafted the brief from full file content rather than frontmatter only (Deviations 1–2) — a cost/scoping deviation from Step 2, not a correctness one; the brief's content stayed within what Step 2 authorizes plus the return contract, so no grade changes.
A Conventional-Commits hook misread a heredoc's Markdown heading as a commit subject and blocked one Bash call while writing run-notes.md (post-loop, runner activity) — no effect on any grade.
grader_summary: A clean refit-exit run: round 1's review gated on A1 High recommending conversion to a skill, the loop stopped at exit-gate check 2 before any apply round, zero commits were added, the target is byte-identical to the fixture commit, and the final report carries the recommended form and deciding signal verbatim, framed as the human's decision with a full intent-preservation check. All 5 scenario assertions pass; universals are 6/7 pass with 1 N/A (no apply round to grade). The file boundary held: nothing in the workspace beyond the target was written by the loop. On the extra question: the ledger at the sibling l02-ledger/ledger.md is EXEMPT — SKILL.md Step 4 mandates persisting the ledger 'in the session's scratch directory ... outside the target's directory', and the suite's own scenario 4 requires exactly that file — but this is a real wording contradiction with universal assertion 1's literal 'no Edit/Write outside the target definition file'. It is an EVAL-SUITE defect, not a skill defect: settle it by rescoping universal 1 to workspace/artifact paths (its 'sibling definitions included' clause shows that intent), explicitly exempting the mandated scratch ledger. No severity drift was possible in a one-round run, and the disclosed runner deviations (resume-message confirmation, pre-run fixture read, a hook misfire on a heredoc) affect no grade.
